step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram and transcript depict a healthcare data integration platform, Lineate Envoy, built on AWS. The flow starts with Lineate's CI/CD pipeline pushing container images to ECR. For runtime, healthcare data ingresses via an NLB, which routes traffic to an EKS cluster running containerized applications on EC2 worker nodes (including Graviton instances). These applications utilize encrypted EBS GP3 volumes for persistent storage. Finally, processed data is delivered to destination healthcare institutions. Nodes were identified based on distinct icons and labels in the diagram, and services were mapped to the exact AWS service names or predefined external actor categories. Edges were drawn strictly following visual arrows for data flow and logical connections described in the transcript, ensuring a sequential flow starting from external actors.

graph.name: Lineate Envoy Healthcare Data Integration Platform
graph.categories: Healthcare, Data Integration, Kubernetes, Cost Optimization, Multi-tenancy
graph.notes: This architecture describes Lineate Envoy, a data integration platform for healthcare. It emphasizes multi-tenant isolation at network, compute, and storage layers, and cost optimization using Graviton EC2 instances and GP3 EBS volumes. The platform is designed to handle HIPAA compliance and geographical data residency requirements by deploying clusters across regions.

nodes.name: Source Healthcare Institution
nodes.notes: Originating healthcare institution sending data to Lineate Envoy.

nodes.name: Network Load Balancer
nodes.notes: Used to expose the data and establish connectivity, handling Layer 4 TCP traffic from healthcare institutions.

nodes.name: Elastic Kubernetes Service
nodes.notes: Envoy is built on Kubernetes, deploying containerized solutions in EKS with dedicated namespaces per customer for tenant isolation. Uses HAProxy as an Ingress Controller.

nodes.name: EC2 Worker Node
nodes.notes: Standard EC2 instances serving as worker nodes for the EKS cluster, hosting containerized applications for Lineate Envoy.

nodes.name: Graviton EC2 Worker Node
nodes.notes: ARM-based Graviton (m6g) EC2 instances, used as worker nodes for EKS to achieve significant cost savings (approx. 20%).

nodes.name: EBS GP3 Volume
nodes.notes: Encrypted GP3 volumes attached to dedicated deployments per customer, ensuring data isolation and providing cost savings. Used for persistent storage by applications.

nodes.name: Elastic Container Registry
nodes.notes: Stores containerized images of integration engines, requirements, and solutions.

nodes.name: Destination Healthcare Institution
nodes.notes: Receiving healthcare institution for processed and transformed data delivered by Lineate Envoy.

nodes.name: Lineate CI/CD
nodes.notes: Represents Lineate's development and CI/CD pipelines responsible for pushing containerized application images.

edges.notes: Lineate's CI/CD pipelines push containerized application images to ECR.
EKS pulls container images from ECR for deploying containerized solutions onto its worker nodes.
EKS deploys and manages containerized applications on EC2 worker nodes.
Healthcare data from institutions is ingressed via the Network Load Balancer (Layer 4 TCP).
NLB routes incoming healthcare data traffic to the EKS cluster (via HAProxy Ingress Controller).
Internal application data flow and communication between containerized applications running on different EC2 worker nodes within the EKS cluster.
Containerized applications on EC2 worker nodes write and store processed data to dedicated EBS GP3 volumes.
Containerized applications on EC2 worker nodes read data from dedicated EBS GP3 volumes for processing.
Processed and transformed healthcare data is delivered from the Envoy platform to the destination healthcare institution.
